<thought>We need to determine the number of CH₃ groups in the compound present in the sample. The most direct way is to retrieve the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample and count the signals that fall in the typical methyl carbon region (≈10–30 ppm). This will give the number of distinct methyl carbons, which corresponds to the number of CH₃ groups unless symmetry makes them equivalent. We'll fetch the carbon NMR data and examine the chemical shift values.</thought>
